decisions.reason: Devore requires specialised burn-out chemistry and finishing knowledge that is likely distant from the firm's existing textile capabilities, limiting its ability to assimilate results and improve the product.
Transparent burnout similarly relies on specialised chemical processing, lowering the firm's absorptive capacity and making continued learning and improvement difficult.
Burnout decorative fabric shares the same specialised process knowledge gap, so the firm is unlikely to interpret early market feedback effectively and should drop it.
Velour-like upholstery builds on the firm's established pile-weaving and finishing know-how, enabling it to learn from early results and improve, so keep.
Flame-retardant interlining requires technical certifications and chemical treatment expertise outside the firm's core, reducing absorptive capacity and increasing drop likelihood.
Polyester satin lining uses standard weaving and finishing skills already present, allowing the firm to interpret feedback and adapt, so keep.
